By mid-to-late June 2026, the relevant bargaining environment is an interim peace/MOU framework involving ceasefire maintenance, Strait of Hormuz reopening, frozen-asset release, sanctions relief, and follow-on nuclear/security negotiations. Diplomatic talks, mediator channels, technical implementation meetings, and asset-release logistics should now be treated as real de-escalatory/substitution-path evidence UNLESS paired with explicit force deployments, ultimatums, or verified ceasefire collapse. Score SubstitutionPath positively when there are verified halt-attack commitments, implementation mechanisms, maritime reopening procedures, demobilization, or mediator-run incident channels. Score CommitmentProblem UPWARD when either side rejects implementation terms, resumes strikes, issues public ultimatums, disputes Hormuz control, or signals that today's deal cannot bind tomorrow's behavior. Score MobilizationSignal or HardlineClaims ONLY for new force movement, alert changes, strike packages, evacuation orders, or concrete operational preparation — NOT for routine rhetoric, accusations, or talk scheduling. PreferenceAlignment fires ONLY on formal structural shifts: deal signed, framework formally collapsed, official MOU withdrawal, or coalition/recognition change. Routine ceasefire violations that are managed within the framework do NOT fire PreferenceAlignment — they fire CommitmentProblem.
